newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -Dlr set to march ahead vs mark, Europeans.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dlr set to march ahead vs mark, Europeans.

text.p: The dollar rocketed to a new near-eight-year peak versus the mark and set multiple-year highs against other European countries with the help of buoyant U.S. economic reports that signaled further gains ahead, analysts said on Friday.
The dollar also took out a key technical resistance level versus the yen but retreated, largely due to the yen's aggressive rebound against the mark.
The upside on dollar/yen appeared far more limited than on dollar/mark, in part due to concern about U.S.-Japan tension possibly developing anew around trade issues, dealers said.

"There is still no sign of a top developing," said senior analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch, referring to dollar/mark's peak at 1.8665 -- the highest since November 1989 when that pair reached a high of 1.8690.
This level is the near-term objective and should offer little resistance, analysts said. The next dollar/mark high dates back to December 1989 when the dollar peaked at 1.9221.

"We closed only 40 ticks below top after the bullish of a week-long symmetric triangle. Clearly, no sign of a top here," stressed Siller who saw an important level at 1.8725, the target in a year-long bull channel projection.
Dollar/mark closed at 1.8620/30 vs. 1.8530/34 at the open, and dollar/yen at 118.35/45 vs. 119.00/05.

The rally's impetus was given early in the session by news 316,000 payroll jobs were created in July while the jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent. Also, U.S. purchasing managers reported a surge in manufacturing activity last month.
Dollar/Paris rose in tandem with dollar/mark to 6.29, its high since November 1989 when it peaked at 6.33, now a target.
Dollar/Swiss set a four-year high at 1.5295, which may point to an attack on 1.5370, a key level in a 10-week bull channel, according to Siller.
"The big story today is that mark/yen fell out of bed," Siller said, commenting on the pullback from 64.45 to a low of 63.53 that broke a bull trend from the July 23 low of 62.92.
Sterling/mark surged as well, past resistance at 3.0300/10, or the 50-percent retracement of the prior high/low retreat from 3.0880 on July 23 to 2.9730 on July 29.

Dollar/yen, much in range-trading, needs to reconquer 119.00, the 50-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move from 126.47 on May 1 to 110.62 on June 11. The next level would be 121 yen, or the 62-percent retracement of that same move and the objective in a rally started in off the June low.
